verdicts.reason: A asserts only that something (some service) is deployed on spire-01, dropping the subject entirely; B asserts the full fact that syncthing specifically is deployed there, in cleft form. B carries the entity identity that A generalises away, and A's existential is a strictly weaker, non-equivalent claim. What would settle it: whether the gold counts an existential generalisation of a named subject as the same proposition rather than a weaker one — the rulebook's own duplicate test is logical equivalence, which these fail.

Both assert exactly that Zulip is deployed on vane-01 — A as a definite predicate nominal ('is the host on which'), B as 'carries the installation'. A's definiteness is presupposed exhaustivity, not asserted content, so neither carries anything the other lacks.

A asserts the deployment of Slurm on yarrow-01 plus a high-availability configuration; B asserts something about yarrow-01's power feed from the rack's secondary PDU. They share only the host name and assert unrelated propositions.

Both assert the same existential: files-01 has at least one deployed component on it. 'has ... deployed on it' and 'carries at least one deployed component' are word-for-word interchangeable in claim content; neither adds anything.

Both assert that anvil-render uses ImageMagick — A in active 'calls on to do its work' phrasing with a sortal ('among the software'), B in the passive. The sortal describes ImageMagick rather than adding a separate claim.

Both assert that ridge-01 uses quire-03; 'is one of the components ridge-01 operates with' and 'is used by ridge-01' are the same relation between the same two entities, with the sortal 'component' carrying no separate claim.

Both assert that Celery is deployed on media-04, each with a definite predicate nominal ('the machine that carries' / 'the host Celery runs on'). Machine and host are the same slot here; nothing is asserted by one and not the other.

A asserts only that alert storms are related to some named component of the estate; B asserts the specific relation between lb-01 and alert storms. B carries the entity lb-01 that A abstracts away, so accepting A does not give you B. What would settle it: whether an existential over the estate counts as the same proposition as the named-entity claim it was weakened from.

A adds a purpose to the use — ClickHouse stores data-06's long-term metrics history; B adds exclusivity — ClickHouse is the only datastore data-06 queries. Each strengthens the premise along a different axis and neither claim contains the other.
A asserts nightly offsite replication of xenon-snapshots; B asserts its exclusion from the last disaster-recovery drill. Two unrelated propositions that share only the entity name.

A asserts that something depends on ledger-02 (existential over dependents); B asserts that clickhouse has some dependency (existential over dependencies). They weaken the premise from opposite ends of the relation, and neither entails the other.

A asserts the full fact that ImageMagick is deployed on images-02; B asserts only that images-02 hosts some deployed component. B drops the subject, so it is a strictly weaker, non-equivalent claim rather than a rewording. What would settle it: whether the gold's 'pure weakening' clause is meant to collapse an existential generalisation into its specific parent proposition.

A asserts a thirty-second polling interval from Uptime Kuma to order-sync; B asserts a nightly volume of several thousand records cleared by order-sync. Different relations, different quantities, no shared claim.

A asserts only that some system uses Authelia; B asserts that auth-02 specifically uses it. B carries the named user that A generalises away. What would settle it: the same question as cases 1 and 12 — whether existential weakening counts as one proposition with its specific source.

A asserts that every request reaching Consul is authenticated through Authelia; B asserts that Authelia enforces two-factor authentication for administrative logins. Different scope, different subject matter — B says nothing about Consul at all.

A asserts that at least one component of the nimbus deployment uses nimbus-archive; B asserts that nimbus-02 specifically uses it. B names the user and A only quantifies over a group, so A is weaker and not equivalent. What would settle it: whether the generalisation from nimbus-02 to 'the nimbus deployment' is treated as a separate scope claim.

A asserts that powerdns uses the fulfillment network for every zone transfer (a universal quantifier over powerdns's transfers); B asserts around-the-clock on-call monitoring of that network. Different relations and different entities doing the acting.

A asserts that ticket-router is deployed on tether-02 (a different host in the same slot); B asserts that wisp-01 runs as a workload on ticket-router (the deployment relation reversed). One is a value swap, the other a direction reversal — different claims that happen to share a verdict.

A asserts only that files-01 has some dependent component in the estate; B asserts that airflow specifically depends on files-01. B carries the dependent's identity that A abstracts away. What would settle it: whether the existential weakening is scored as the same proposition as the named-pair fact.

Both assert that ledger-02 causes mon-05 — A via a definite predicate nominal ('the effect that ledger-02 produces'), B via 'is brought about by'. Under the rulebook's exhaustivity rule the definite nominal presupposes rather than asserts sole-effect status, so nothing separate is claimed; a reader who took 'the effect' as asserting uniqueness would call them distinct, and that reading is what would settle it.
Both assert that nimbus-02 uses RabbitMQ; 'is used by' and 'is called on by' are the same relation between the same two entities with no difference in strength or scope.

Both render the same use relation between osquery and quota-watcher — A as 'osquery's operation involves' it, B as 'a component that osquery relies on'. Borderline because 'relies on' carries a dependence flavour that bare involvement does not; what would settle it is whether this gold treats reliance as strictly stronger than use, in which case B asserts something A does not.

A asserts that idx-03 hosts some deployed service (dropping Meilisearch); B asserts that Meilisearch is deployed on some host (dropping idx-03). Each weakens away the entity the other keeps, and neither entails the other.

A asserts that ledger-02 sits in the finance team's rack allocation, saying nothing about CockroachDB; B asserts the deployment plus that ledger-02 is provisioned as a dedicated database host. Different added content and different subject matter.
